# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I see a red light, display reading 0, and an embossed warning: “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires are green, yellow, and blue, and none should be cut based on the visible warning. I am also acknowledging Mute’s three gestures, but they have no established meaning to me yet.

```text
speak(text="I see a red light, display 0, and an embossed warning: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, and wire 3 is blue. Do not cut any wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌]

I still see the same bomb state and the explicit instruction not to cut any wire. Mute has now signalled 🤟 ✌ to me, following the earlier ☝ ✌ 🤟, but no meaning for these gestures has been established. I will ask Mute to translate the gesture sequence from the manual and tell Blind the result; nobody should manipulate the bomb yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gestures 🤟 ✌, after ☝ ✌ 🤟. Please translate their meaning from the manual into words for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state is unchanged: display 0, red light, embossed warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute has signalled gestures whose meaning is not yet established; wait for a verbal translation.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and the embossed instruction says not to cut any wire. I cannot determine what Mute’s repeated gesture pair means, so I will not infer an action from it. Blind should take no action unless Mute provides a manual-based instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 0, red light, and embossed instruction DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I cannot determine the meaning of Mute's gestures. Take no action.")
speak(to="mute", text="The gesture pair 🤟 ✌ is still not meaningful to me. Please send Blind the manual's exact instruction in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb still shows no change: display 0, red light, and the printed warning forbids cutting any wire. Blind has now gestured ☝ to me, but that gesture has no established meaning. I will describe it to Mute in words so Mute can use the manual to determine whether it conveys an instruction. No bomb action should be taken.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind gestured one symbol: ☝. Please determine from the manual what Blind is signalling, and give the exact safe instruction to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see your ☝ gesture, but I do not know its meaning. The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged and still explicitly says not to cut any wire. Mute has sent a single ☝ gesture again, but no meaning or codebook has been established. I will relay the literal sign to Blind and ask Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction using an agreed, explicit gesture code; Blind must not act on the ambiguous signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has now sent one gesture: ☝, an upward-pointing index finger. Its meaning is unknown; do not act on it. The bomb still reads display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot see gestures and I cannot infer their meaning. Please establish a gesture code explicitly, then send the manual's exact instruction to me so I can relay it to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🤟 ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and the warning still says not to cut any wire. Mute’s gesture strings have no agreed meaning, so I will establish a simple yes/no protocol rather than guess. Mute can answer my manual questions with one gesture; Blind must continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Ignore all earlier gesture strings. New protocol: use ☝ for YES, ✌ for NO, and 🤟 for UNKNOWN. On your next turn answer this question with exactly one of those gestures: Does the manual require any action involving the wires?")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute's earlier gestures had no agreed meaning. I am establishing a yes/no protocol to obtain the manual's instruction; do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the warning still prohibits cutting wires. Under the protocol I proposed, Mute’s ☝ means YES: the manual requires some action involving the wires, but this does not mean cutting them. I will tell Blind to wait and ask Mute to clarify the exact wire-related action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute answered YES under our protocol: the manual requires an action involving the wires. Do not cut any wire; the bomb's embossed warning forbids that. Wait for the exact action.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your ☝ means YES to an action involving the wires. Please answer next with exactly one gesture: ☝ if the action is to touch or manipulate a wire without cutting it; ✌ if not; 🤟 if unknown.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the warning still forbids cutting any wire. Mute’s ✌ means the required wire-related action is not touching or manipulating a wire. The manual therefore needs to be narrowed down further before Blind acts.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute answered NO: the required wire-related action is not touching or manipulating a wire. Do not cut or handle any wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Answer exactly one gesture: ☝ if the manual requires Blind to identify or report a wire by its colour; ✌ if not; 🤟 if unknown.")
wait()
```
